episodes.title: Brain Fog, Part 1 - Is Your Brain in a Fog?

description.full:
Dr. David Musnick (Dr. M), board-certified in Internal Medicine and Sports Medicine with 35+ years in regenerative and functional medicine, dives straight into one of the most common complaints he sees: brain fog.

Discover what brain fog really feels like—slow thinking, low mental energy, word-finding trouble, poor focus, memory slips—and why it’s not normal at any age. Learn the core mechanisms (brain inflammation, dysfunctional microglia, neurotransmitter issues) and why ignoring it can lead to headaches, chronic fatigue, cognitive decline, and more.

Dr. M outlines a long but eye-opening list of potential causes: excitotoxins (MSG & aspartame), poor oxygen delivery, concussions, gluten/autoimmunity, blood sugar swings, hormones, mold, infections (EBV, Lyme, long COVID), heavy metals, EMFs, medications, and more.

Get practical first steps to fight back:

  • Eat organic, grass-fed, add parsley (for apigenin to calm microglia)
  • Prioritize 7.5+ hours of quality sleep
  • Exercise daily to boost BDNF
  • Reduce EMFs (WiFi off at night, phone away from head)
  • Avoid plastics and hidden toxins

He stresses finding root causes with functional testing rather than masking symptoms. Perfect for anyone feeling mentally sluggish—whether post-viral, stressed, or just “not sharp.”

Part 2 (coming soon) covers advanced evaluation and targeted treatments.

Short, direct, mechanism-focused. Subscribe for more no-fluff insights on brain, gut, immune, and regenerative health from FMI Center for Optimal Health.

#BrainFog #FunctionalMedicine #BrainHealth #CognitiveHealth

episodes.title: Brain Fog, Part 2 - Testing and Basic Solutions

description.full:
Dr. David Musnick M.D. (Dr. M), board-certified in Internal Medicine & Sports Medicine, picks up right where Brain Fog Part 1 left off in this ~20-minute solo episode.

Quick recap: Brain fog = brain dysfunction with inflammation, slowed neurotransmission, and that classic “slow, foggy, not sharp” feeling. Simple/occasional fog is concerning; when it comes with memory issues, poor focus, word-finding trouble, or speech problems, it’s much more serious. Episodes >15–20 minutes (vs. fleeting) warrant extra attention. Part 1 covered a broad list of triggers: brain inflammation, food allergies, EMFs, heavy metals, Lyme/co-infections, viruses, brain autoimmunity, and beyond.

Part 2 answers: Which tests make sense? And what foundational steps help almost everyone?

Recommended Tests

  • Inflammation markers (systemic inflammation often fuels brain inflammation & fog):
  • Epstein-Barr reactivation (common hidden driver of brain fog & “brain fatigue” where mental tasks drain you quickly):Full panel required (not basic EBV test):• VCA IgG & IgM• EBNA• Early Antigen (EA)Any marker ≥8× upper normal limit signals reactivation—needs functional treatment (no standard antiviral drug exists).
  • Mold/mycotoxins (if exposure suspected): Urine mycotoxin panel (e.g., Mosaic Diagnostics, RealTime Labs, others).
  • Other blood clues: Homocysteine (elevated harms brain vessels).
  • Imaging: Brain MRI not typically first-line unless severe/progressive cognitive changes or neurological red flags.

Dr. M emphasizes: Pinpoint and treat root causes (e.g., reactivated viruses, mold, infections) with a knowledgeable functional medicine or functional neurology provider. Cause-specific care is key—general “brain fog fixes” alone won’t cut it if Lyme, EBV, or mycotoxins are driving it.

Universal Basics to Start TodayWhile hunting the root cause, layer in these brain-protective steps (many from Part 1): prioritize 7.5+ hours quality sleep, daily exercise to raise BDNF, organic/grass-fed foods, parsley (apigenin to calm microglia), EMF reduction (WiFi off at night), avoid plastics/excitotoxins, and more.

Direct, practical, mechanism-focused—no long intros or filler. Perfect if you’re dealing with persistent mental cloudiness, post-viral fatigue, or just want sharper thinking.

Part 3 or future episodes may cover targeted treatments for big culprits like Epstein-Barr.

Subscribe for concise, experience-based insights on brain, immune, gut, and regenerative health from FMI Center for Optimal Health in Eagle, Idaho.

#BrainFog #FunctionalMedicine #EpsteinBarr #Mycotoxins #BrainHealth

description.full:

episodes.title: Electromagnetic Frequencies (EMF) - Practical Ways to Reduce Exposure

description.full:
🛡️ Protect Your Brain from EMF, WiFi & 5G Exposure | Practical Tips from Dr. David Musnick MD

In Episode 4 of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, board-certified Sports & Functional Medicine physician Dr. David Musnick reveals how everyday electromagnetic fields are silently affecting your brain and body — and what you can do about it right now.

You’ll learn the 3 main types of exposure on the electromagnetic spectrum:

  • Radio Frequency (RF) – the most common and damaging (cell phones, WiFi, Bluetooth, 5G towers, wireless earbuds)
  • Electromagnetic Fields (EMF) – from appliances, EVs, hybrids, and plugged-in devices
  • Electrical Fields – from home wiring

Dr. Musnick explains how these fields can disrupt the blood-brain barrier, leading to brain fog, headaches, migraines, inflammation, insomnia, and even increased risk of autoimmunity. He also connects poor sleep to a “leaky brain” and why protecting this barrier is critical for long-term brain health.

Actionable Mitigation Strategies Covered:

  • Switch to wired keyboards, mice & air-tube headsets instead of Bluetooth
  • Put your phone in airplane mode (or keep it 10+ feet away) while sleeping
  • Hardwire your home with Ethernet and turn WiFi off at night (“friends don’t let friends sleep with WiFi”)
  • Turn Bluetooth & WiFi off on phones/iPads when not in use
  • Test cars (especially electric & hybrid vehicles) with a meter before buying
  • Opt out of smart meters or shield them
  • Use accurate meters like the Safe and Sound II and Tri-Field meter to measure your home, car, and workplace
  • Consider shielded clothing, Airs Tech scalar devices, or professional home assessments if you’re sensitive

Whether you’re experiencing unexplained headaches, fatigue, or brain fog — or you simply want to safeguard your family in our wireless world — this short, practical episode gives you the tools to reduce exposure starting today.

📌 Resources & Links (meters, shielding products, smart meter guards, Airs Tech, etc.) are in the pinned comment and show notes.

episodes.title: Energy - Understanding Fatigue and Mitochondrial Health

description.full:
In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M takes a deep dive into energy, fatigue, and mitochondrial health. He explains why fatigue is often more complex than “just being tired,” exploring possible contributors such as poor sleep, sleep apnea, inflammation, viral reactivation, Lyme and co-infections, mold exposure, heavy metals, hormone imbalances, adrenal and thyroid function, liver and kidney stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction.

Dr. M also discusses practical ways to support energy production, including grounding, improving sleep, supporting ATP production, methylated B vitamins, magnesium, zinc, copper, CoQ10, NAD support, PQQ, and methylene blue. This episode is packed with functional medicine insights for anyone looking to better understand the many factors that can affect daily energy, vitality, and resilience.

This episode is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for personalized medical care. Always consult your own healthcare provider before making changes to your health plan, testing, or supplements.

episodes.title: Concussion - What Happens in the Brain

description.full:
In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. David Musnick takes a deep dive into concussion, traumatic brain injury, and the functional medicine mechanisms behind brain injury recovery. Drawing on decades of experience in sports medicine and functional medicine, Dr. M explains why concussion care should go beyond simply ruling out a brain bleed and telling someone to rest.

This episode explores what actually happens in the brain after a concussion, including structural injury, neural shearing, excitotoxicity, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, hypoxia, blood-brain barrier disruption, brain autoimmunity, hormone dysfunction, pituitary involvement, vagus nerve dysfunction, mitochondrial dysfunction, protein folding abnormalities, neurogenesis, synaptogenesis, and gut microbiome changes.

Dr. M also discusses why symptoms such as brain fog, headache, dizziness, emotional instability, fatigue, sleepiness, and brain-based fatigue can persist after a head injury — even when the person never directly hit their head. This episode sets the foundation for future conversations on how to address the pathways involved in concussion recovery.

This episode is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for personalized medical care. Always consult your own healthcare provider for diagnosis, treatment, testing, supplements, or return-to-play decisions after a concussion or head injury.

episodes.websiteSummary: Dr. Musnick explains concussion and traumatic brain injury mechanisms, from neural shearing, excitotoxicity, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, hypoxia, and blood-brain barrier disruption to persistent symptoms and recovery pathways.
